messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Introductory NIMBLE Workshop, Switzerland, April 2018
parts:
Dear all,

 

from 23-25 April 2018 Michael Schaub and I are hosting a Nimble introductory workshop taught by Perry de Valpine (University of California, Berkeley), see attachment and also here: http://www.phidot.org/forum/viewtopic.php?f=8&t=3586

 

Nimble is the latest member of the software family for fitting hierarchical models that uses the BUGS language to describe the model. In our opinion this is almost a prerequisite for wide adoption by ecologist and other non-statisticians. Nimble offers exciting capabilities to extend the functionality, customize the MCMC samplers and allows fitting of hierarchical models by likelihood methods.

 

Best regards  --- Marc Kéry

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: FW: Introductory NIMBLE Workshop, Switzerland, April 2018
parts:
Hi all.

I forward a short description of the capabilities of the new Nimble software just posted in the HMecology google group.

Best regards  --- Marc
From: Perry de Valpine [pdeva...@berkeley.edu]
Sent: 12 January 2018 18:51
To: Tomas Telensky
Cc: Kery Marc; hmec...@googlegroups.com; unmarked
Subject: Re: Introductory NIMBLE Workshop, Switzerland, April 2018

In a nutshell: NIMBLE makes both the BUGS model language and algorithms that use models extensible.  You can add new functions and distributions.  You can customize choice of samplers, write new samplers, and write/use other methods (not just MCMC).  Models and algorithms are compiled by generating and compiling C++, so everything can run fast.  We do have relatively new support for CAR models, and there is room for anyone to contribute improved general or case-specific methods.  If you write something that you want to share, you can contribute to NIMBLE or write your own R package that uses NIMBLE.  Something like BART regression trees would be an interesting case for adding new functions, distributions and samplers to support these models.  If there are external libraries you want to use, you can have the compiled NIMBLE code call externally compiled code.  For more information (including a full user manual), please see http:r-nimble.org

While I have the floor: we are hiring a post-doc!  Please see https://r-nimble.org/nimble-has-a-post-doc-or-software-developer-position-open

Perry
